item.title: City commissioners start process to consider annexing land west of K-10 into Lawrence
item.description: Lawrence city commissioners voted Tuesday to begin the process to consider potentially annexing 650 acres of land west of K-10 — about 1 square mile — into city limits Continue reading ...

item.title: Kansas Senate votes to subvert students’ First Amendment right to join public protests
item.description: The Kansas Senate voted Tuesday to clamp down on public school protests by requiring students to secure parental permission to participate and by imposing penalties on districts complicit in organizing protests or meek in disciplining student offenders. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence city commissioners vote to keep Community Building free to use for 3 more months
item.description: The Community Building and its exercise and free play facilities will remain free for the public to use for another three months following the Lawrence City Commission's 4-1 vote on Tuesday. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence City Commission general public comment for March 3, 2026
item.description: Here’s the general public comment for the Lawrence City Commission’s Tuesday meeting, as public comment is no longer being broadcast. Continue reading ...

item.title: Kansas lawmakers want to legalize silencers and sawed-off shotguns
item.description: Owning firearm suppressors or sawed-off shotguns is legal federally, but not in Kansas. Some state lawmakers are trying to change that, but multiple law enforcement organizations have come out against the bill. Continue reading ...

item.title: Bert Nash panel series to highlight women’s mental health

item.title: Lawrence Transit announces proposed route changes, seeks public feedback

item.title: KU faculty union rallies as bargaining team meets with administrators, hoping to avoid impasse
item.description: Members of the KU faculty union protested outside of Wescoe Hall Wednesday while the union bargaining team met with administrators for last-minute contract talks, hoping to avoid an impasse. Continue reading ...

item.title: KU governance asks community to vote on whether they have confidence in chancellor, CFO
item.description: KU staff and students will voice whether they have confidence in the leadership of Chancellor Doug Girod, after the presidents of the Faculty Senate and University Senate initiated a vote this week amid concerns over the financial health of KU. Continue reading ...

item.title: Kansans can’t use food assistance to buy candy, soda beginning in February 2027
item.description: Kansans receiving food assistance can’t buy soda or candy with those dollars beginning in 2027, Gov. Laura Kelly said Wednesday. Continue reading ...
